
### Addresses in the Target Code for the Notes of the Unit 5 - Code Generation in the Subject of Compiler Design

* Addresses in the target code are used to store the locations of instructions and data in the memory. 
* Addresses are used to refer to the location of instructions and data in the target code.
* Addresses are generated by the compiler and are represented as numbers.
* Addresses are usually represented in hexadecimal format.
* The compiler generates the addresses in the target code by assigning a unique address to each instruction and data item.
* The compiler assigns the addresses in the target code based on the size of the instruction and data items.
* The compiler also takes into account the alignment requirements of the target code.
* The addresses in the target code are used to refer to the instructions and data items in the memory.
* Addresses in the target code are also used to refer to the locations of labels, variables and constants.
* The addresses in the target code are used to access the instructions and data in the memory.
* The addresses in the target code are also used to refer to the locations of jump instructions and subroutines.
* The addresses in the target code are used to determine the flow of the program.
